title: Midloop triage — spot check & TODOs
content:
Quick midloop notes (11:30-12:15) — for my personal triage. Do not copy/paste into PR without running local repros.

Context:
- Observed intermittent p99 spikes on the small-inference fleet starting 07-17 22:40 UTC. Baseline p99 ~35ms, spikes to ~220-270ms for a subset of short requests (~<=128 tokens).
- Affected shard pool: pool-small-g5-3. Pattern: spikes appear after a burst of concurrent requests (~120 concurrent) and settle after ~30s.
- Dashboard traces show long time spent in kv cache miss path + cpu time in kernel lock contended section.

Quick observations from logs:
- repeated lines: "kv_cache: lookup miss seq_len=64 keyhash=0x3a2f" interleaved with "batcher: flush delayed (window=12ms)"
- Several processes reported transient EPIPE then recovered — likely early socket close from client when latency >200ms.
- Allocation histograms show small tail increase in CPU sys time on worker threads vs user time.

Repro attempts (local/ci):
1) Local microbench replicating burst (ab-style): 200 concurrent, payload=prompt-short.json -> reproduced p99 ~180ms but not 250ms.
2) Added artificial jitter to request arrival (poisson) -> made p99 worse in local run (200->240ms).
3) Disabled prefix caching -> p99 drops to ~60ms but overall throughput decreases.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: KV cache lock contention under bursted access pattern. Lock's hold time increases when many misses trigger async loads.
- H2: Batcher flush policy degenerates when many small windows align, causing repeated micro-flushes and kernel context churn.
- H3: Memory allocator fragmentation on small buffers -> increase in syscalls/alloc leading to cpu sys spike.
- H4: Rare slow device IO path (host<->gpu transfer) triggered by specific key sequences (sequence length edge-case).

Quick experiments I ran and notes:
- Added fine-grained timing around kv cache lock (enter/exit) -> average hold time 0.42ms normally, during spike jumps to 3.8ms. This correlates with bursts.
- Switched batcher policy: from dynamic-window to fixed 8ms -> p99 improved but throughput regressed by ~10%. Good signal that batching interplay matters.
- Tried jemalloc tuning (background threads on) -> small improvement on p99 tail. Suggests allocator plays a role but not primary.

Immediate TODOs (order matters):
- [P0] Add lock-free read path for kv-cache lookup to reduce contention on hits. Minimal change: attempt optimistic read, fallback to lock for miss. (owner: Mira) Target: quick spike mitigation.
- [P0] Roll local fixed-window batcher experiment into canary for pool-small-g5-3 for 2h. Watch p99, throughput, error rates. (owner: Kai)
- [P1] Add metrics: kv_cache.lock_hold_ms histogram per shard, batcher.flush_count_per_sec. (owner: Mira)
- [P1] Create a small alloc profile snapshot during spike windows (perf + pprof) and upload to ticket. (owner: Noor)
- [P2] Run a longer run (12h) with prefix-caching disabled in a single canary to understand throughput tradeoffs. (owner: Mira)

Quick mitigation plan if spike recurs (manual):
- Temporarily route traffic from pool-small-g5-3 -> pool-small-fallback (lower concurrency limit) via smart-routing. Ops runbook reference: PRUNE-traffic-ops.docx (quick link in slack).
- Increase batcher min-window to 8ms to reduce microflush churn.
- If we see EPIPE increase, short circuit prefix-caching for 60s on the shard.

Questions to raise in perf sync (tomorrow):
- Can we get a microbench harness that reproduces optimistic read vs locked read at scale (~1k concurrent) on our infra?
- Is there an existing lock-free helper we can reuse from platform-engineering? (ask Noah?)
- Long term: should kv-cache be sharded by keyhash to avoid single lock hot spot? Cost: increased memory footprint.

Logs / artifacts to attach to ticket RINF-3421:
- local-run-flaky-p99-2025-07-18.tar.gz (pprof, perf stat logs)
- trace snippets from console (span IDs in slack thread)
- kv_cache lock timings csv (small)

Hand-off notes for after lunch (if I step out):
- If canary shows >20% p99 regression vs baseline, rollback batcher policy to dynamic-window and revert commit 3f4c2b.
- If lock hold >1.5ms on average for >60s, enable 'kv_cache_opt_read' flag (feature-flagged) which was merged in experimental branch (PR 887).
- Keep Noor looped for allocator profile upload.

Commands / quick snippets I used (for reference):
- reproducer: ./tools/bench --concurrency 200 --payload test_prompts/short.json --poisson
- pprof capture: curl localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > p.prof
- lock timing: grep kv_cache_lock *.log | awk '{print $NF}' | python -c 'import sys; print(sorted([float(l) for l in sys.stdin.read().splitlines()])[-20:])'

Notes to self (bullet brain dump):
- Don't conflate allocator noise with lock contention; look at sys vs user CPU per-thread.
- Edge-case: seq_len >1024 seemed to correlate in one trace; add a test with mixed seq lengths.
- Check whether client SDK retries are bubbling up and creating request storms (rate-limiter misconfigured?).

EOD checklist (for me):
- push small metric PR (kv lock histogram) -> done? verify in staging.
- open a short explainer for PMs: 1-pager on batching + kv tradeoffs. (start draft)
- update RINF-3421 with canary results and attach pprof.

Random thought: Could use a tiny bounded MPSC queue per worker to smooth arrivals before kv cache lookup, then pull from queue in small batches. Might reduce contention without changing global batcher. Worth mocking in local harness.

— Mira
